resources.string:
Fill the grid so that every row, every column and every 3×3 box contains the digits 1 to 9 once each. The pre-filled digits cannot be changed.

Tap a cell, then a digit on the pad to place it. Or tap a digit first, then tap several cells to fill them with it. The Notes button lets you jot small candidate digits in a cell, and Undo takes back your last digit.

In Easy, mistakes and clashes show up as you play. In Medium and Hard, use the Check button to see them for a moment. A hint costs 5 neutrinos and fills one cell; using one means no reward for that grid.

Swipe to slide all the tiles in one direction. When two tiles with the same number touch, they merge into one tile with their sum, and your score goes up. A new tile appears after each move.

Choose the grid size (3×3 to 6×6) and the target tile. Reach it to win a universe and earn neutrinos; if the grid is stuck, you lose it. A new game starts by itself.

Quantum mode adds an odd target and a few cat jokers. Press the joker, then swipe: any two neighbouring tiles can merge, even with different numbers. You can also drag one tile onto its neighbour to merge just those two.

Uncover every square that hides no mine. The first tap is always safe.

Tap a hidden square to uncover it. A number tells how many mines touch that square, including diagonals. Touch and hold a square to place or remove a flag where you think a mine is.

Tap a number whose flags already match its count to uncover all its other neighbours at once. Touching a mine ends the game. Pick the difficulty at the top: a bigger grid with more mines is harder, and the best times are kept.

Push every crate onto a glowing dock. You are the robot: you can push one crate at a time and never pull it, so think before you push, because a crate in a corner is stuck for good.

Swipe on the board to move, or use the arrows. Undo takes back your last move, Restart puts the puzzle back at the start and New draws another one.

The counters show your moves and pushes, and the challenge gives the smallest number of pushes. Your best score is kept for each difficulty.

Swap two neighbouring pieces to line up at least three identical ones. Swipe a piece, or tap two pieces. Matches disappear and others fall in their place.

Tilt your device to choose the direction pieces fall, even during cascades. Four in a row clears the whole line; an L or a T explodes around the junction.

In the forge modes, reach the goal of each board before you run out of moves: collect a metal, clean slag or deliver a core to its green exit. Only a successful swap costs a move. In Overheat, race the clock: each match gives time back.

Sort the tokens so that every column holds only one colour, completely filled. An empty column is a good place to park tokens.

Tap a column to pick up its top token, then tap another column to drop it. You can drop it on an empty column or on a token of the same colour, as long as there is room.

Touch and hold a column to move the whole group of same-coloured tokens at the top at once. Undo takes back your last move, Restart goes back to the start, New makes another game. Easy, Medium and Hard add columns and colours.

Turn the rings so that every ring shows the same colour in each of the six slices, as if they were one single disc.

Place your finger on a ring and slide it around to turn it. Careful: some rings are linked, and turning one also turns its partner, shown by a bridge between them.

The counter shows your moves. Hint plays one good move for you, but then the game gives no neutrinos. Restart goes back to the start, and the difficulty chips set the number of rings.

Every cell is an excited atom, and its number tells how many times it must still be touched before it rests at zero. Bring all the atoms to rest.

To place a piece from your hand, slide your finger over neighbouring cells to draw its shape, then lift. You can draw a piece in any orientation, and a piece that would push an atom below zero is refused.

Twin atoms, joined by a coloured wire, share their fate: touching one also lowers the other, wherever it is. Each floor you finish gives points, fewer if you undo or restart. Clear all 15 floors, the last one is the boss, to win neutrinos from your total score.

Turn the pipes so that water reaches every pipe from the source.

Tap a pipe to turn it a quarter turn. The status panel shows how many pipes are already wet. When all of them are connected, the puzzle is solved and you earn neutrinos.

The chips choose the grid size, from 4×4 to 8×8. The moves and the time are counted, but nothing limits you.

Trace: draw one single path from the first numbered pad to the last one. It must go through the pads in order (1, 2, 3…) and fill every free square of the board.

Wiring: link each pair of same-coloured connectors with a wire. Wires cannot cross, and together they must fill the whole board.

Put your finger on the start and slide it along the squares. Slide back to shorten a path, or touch a path to cut it from there. The clear button wipes all your traces. Easy, Medium and Hard change the board size, and your level goes up with each success.

Link the stars with straight lines to draw one single constellation. Each star shows how many links it needs, with small lights around it that turn on as you go.

Put your finger on a star and slide towards another one: the line goes to the nearest visible star in that direction. To remove a line, slide along it or touch it. Two lines can never cross, and two stars share at most one line.

You win when every star has exactly its number of links and all of them are joined together. The new constellation gets a name and goes into your sky atlas. The chips choose the size, and the circular arrow clears all the lines.

Sneak through the maze, collect every amber crystal, then reach the exit. The exit does not open until you have all of them.

Swipe to move one square, tap to wait one turn. Each action is a turn, and the guards move one step on every turn. They watch the coral squares in front of them: if you step on one, or run into a guard, you are caught and you tap to try again.

Watch the patrols and time your moves. Finish in the optimal number of turns for a perfect escape and double neutrinos. The difficulty buttons change the maze.
